newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: DCP sees higher earnings in second half.
newsitem.headline: DCP sees higher earnings in second half.

text.p: Direct Capital Partners Ltd said on Friday it expects earnings fron associate companies to increase in the second half of the 1996/97 financial year.
DCP reported a net profit of NZ$3.65 million for the six months to December 31, up from $3.45 million in the comparable year-ago period.

DCP said earnings from investments in associate companies in the first half result were $0.53 million compared with $0.48 million. Earnings from associates are derived through equity accounted earnings and dividends received.
DCP said it had made four new investments since the June 30 year-end balance date and appropriate unlisted company investment opportunities continued to be put before the company.

"With an improved trading outlook for the existing investees and the four new investments being accounted for the full second half year period, directors expect earnings from associate companies to increase on the second half year," DCP said.
